facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of a painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone
the mass measured approximately 4.0 × 3.5 cm
was well circumscribed, soft, nonmobile, and non-tender
Laboratory studies and neurologic examination were unremarkable
a large, circumscribed radiolucent lesion in the right frontal bone without adjacent soft-tissue swelling
a lytic lesion of the frontal bone with a soap-bubble appearance, cortical destruction of the inner and outer tables, and an associated soft-tissue component
a lobulated frontal-bone mass measuring 3.7 × 3.3 × 2.8 cm
was hypointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and showed avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences

concepts.why: The patient presents with a painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone, and radiography shows a circumscribed radiolucent lesion in the right frontal bone.
The mass is well circumscribed, soft, nonmobile, and non-tender, and CT of the head demonstrates a lytic lesion of the frontal bone with a soap-bubble appearance.
The lobulated frontal-bone mass is hypointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and shows avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences.

rationales.F01: Painless mass is more typical of benign bone tumors like osteoma
rationales.F03: Well-circumscribed and non-tender mass is less typical of brown tumor
rationales.F04: Unremarkable laboratory studies and neurologic examination make brown tumor less likely
rationales.F05: Circumscribed radiolucent lesion is consistent with osteoma or fibrous dysplasia
rationales.F06: Lytic lesion with soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction is more typical of fibrous dysplasia or brown tumor
rationales.F08: Avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences is more typical of fibrous dysplasia or brown tumor

frontier_selector.rationale: The soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction of the inner and outer tables are characteristic of fibrous dysplasia, and the lack of significant laboratory or neurologic findings also supports this diagnosis.
